description: Black gram (urad, minumulu) is a short-duration pulse grown in kharif, rabi and in the rice fallows of coastal Andhra Pradesh. It fixes its own nitrogen and needs only a small starter dose with phosphorus.
npk_split: Apply all N and P as basal at sowing, add potash only where the soil test shows low potassium, and treat the seed with Rhizobium culture.

Anthracnose.name: Anthracnose
Anthracnose.description: A seed-borne fungal disease that spots the leaves and pods in cool, wet weather. Early infection kills seedlings and later infection gives spotted pods with shrivelled seed.
symptoms: Round dark brown sunken spots with a dark centre and bright red-orange margin on leaves and pods
Spot centres fall out leaving shot-holes
Seedlings blighted soon after emergence
Spotted pods with shrivelled seed
Anthracnose.spread: Carried by infected seed and crop debris and spread by rain splash in cool, wet weather.
Anthracnose.action: Spray mancozeb 75 WP 2.5 g/L or carbendazim 50 WP 1 g/L at the first spots and repeat after 15 days.

treatment.name: Mancozeb 75 WP
treatment.notes: Protective spray; repeat after 15 days in wet weather.

treatment.name: Carbendazim 50 WP seed treatment
treatment.notes: Use seed from a healthy crop and treat before sowing.

Cercospora leaf spot.name: Cercospora Leaf Spot
Cercospora leaf spot.description: A common fungal leaf spot of black gram that builds up in humid weather from about 30 days after sowing. Heavy spotting at flowering and pod stage causes leaf fall and lower yield.
symptoms: Small round spots with grey-white centre and reddish-brown margin
Many spots merge into irregular dead patches
Leaves dry and drop at flowering and pod formation
Similar spots on stems and pods
Cercospora leaf spot.spread: Survives on crop debris and seed and spreads by wind and rain splash in humid weather.
Cercospora leaf spot.action: Spray carbendazim 50 WP 1 g/L or mancozeb 75 WP 2.5 g/L at the first spots and repeat after 15 days.

treatment.name: Carbendazim 50 WP
treatment.notes: First spray at about 30 days after sowing or at first spots.

treatment.name: Mancozeb 75 WP
treatment.notes: Alternate with carbendazim for the second spray.

Insect damage.name: Insect Damage
Insect damage.cause: Chewing or sucking insects of unspecified species (e.g. Spodoptera litura, Maruca vitrata, leaf beetles, aphids, thrips)
Insect damage.description: Leaf injury caused by insects; the photo shows the damage but not which insect did it. Check the plant to see whether caterpillars, beetles or small sucking insects are present before choosing a spray.
symptoms: Holes or ragged, chewed leaf edges
Scraped or skeletonised patches where only veins remain
Leaves and flowers webbed together with droppings inside
Curled or speckled leaves with small insects on the underside
Insect damage.spread: Adult insects fly in from neighbouring crops and weeds and multiply quickly in warm weather.
Insect damage.action: Turn over the leaves to find which insect is feeding, hand-pick caterpillars and egg masses, and spray neem oil 1500 ppm 5 ml/L if damage is spreading.

treatment.name: Neem oil 1500 ppm
treatment.notes: First spray for light damage by any insect; spray in the evening.

treatment.name: Chlorantraniliprole 18.5 SC
treatment.notes: Only if caterpillars (Spodoptera, spotted pod borer) are found feeding.

treatment.name: Thiamethoxam 25 WG
treatment.notes: Only if aphids, whiteflies or thrips are found on the underside of leaves; toxic to bees - do not spray on open flowers; only where the label lists your crop.

Leaf crinkle virus.name: Leaf Crinkle Virus
Leaf crinkle virus.description: A mainly seed-borne virus disease that makes the leaves large, thick and crinkled and stops the flowers from setting pods. There is no curative spray, and plants infected early give almost no yield.
symptoms: Leaves larger than normal, thick and crinkled
Puckered, wavy leaf surface that is lighter green
Stunted, bushy plant
Flower buds malformed and remain closed, very few pods
Leaf crinkle virus.spread: Comes mainly through infected seed and is spread further by sap contact and insects such as aphids.
Leaf crinkle virus.action: Pull out and destroy crinkled plants as soon as they are seen, within 45 days of sowing, and do not save seed from this field.

treatment.name: Roguing and clean seed
treatment.notes: No spray cures the virus; buy certified seed or take seed only from a crop that showed no crinkle.

treatment.name: Imidacloprid 17.8 SL
treatment.notes: Vector control only, when aphids are seen on the young crop; toxic to bees - do not spray on open flowers; only where the label lists your crop.

Powdery mildew.name: Powdery Mildew
Powdery mildew.description: A fungal disease that covers leaves, stems and pods with white powder, mainly in rabi and rice-fallow crops. It forces early maturity and reduces pod filling.
symptoms: White powdery patches on the upper leaf surface
Powder spreads to stems and pods
Leaves turn yellow, then brown, and drop
Crop matures early with small seed
Powdery mildew.spread: Airborne spores spread fast in cool, dry weather, especially on late-sown crops.
Powdery mildew.action: Spray wettable sulphur 80 WP 3 g/L or hexaconazole 5 EC 2 ml/L at the first white patches and repeat after 10-15 days.

treatment.name: Wettable sulphur 80 WP
treatment.notes: Cover both leaf surfaces; do not spray in very hot afternoon sun.

treatment.name: Hexaconazole 5 EC
treatment.notes: Use if the disease is already well established.

Yellow mosaic virus.name: Yellow Mosaic Virus
Yellow mosaic virus.cause: Mungbean yellow mosaic virus / Mungbean yellow mosaic India virus (begomovirus)
Yellow mosaic virus.description: The most destructive disease of black gram, carried by whitefly. There is no curative spray, and plants infected before flowering give few, small pods with shrivelled seed.
symptoms: Scattered small yellow specks on young leaves
Bright yellow and green mosaic patches that enlarge
Whole leaf turns yellow and later papery white
Stunted plants with few, small, yellow pods
Yellow mosaic virus.spread: Spread by whiteflies from infected plants and weed hosts; it is not carried by seed or soil.
Yellow mosaic virus.action: Pull out yellow plants up to 40 days after sowing and spray thiamethoxam 25 WG 0.3 g/L to check whiteflies.

treatment.name: Resistant varieties
treatment.notes: Grow yellow mosaic resistant or tolerant varieties such as PU 31, LBG 787, TBG 104 or VBN 8; this is the most reliable control.

treatment.name: Thiamethoxam 25 WG
treatment.notes: Vector control only; spray when whiteflies are seen and repeat after 10-15 days if they return, not more than 2 sprays a season; toxic to bees - do not spray on open flowers; only where the label lists your crop.

treatment.name: Acetamiprid 20 SP
treatment.notes: Alternative for whitefly, but the same group (IRAC 4A neonicotinoid) as thiamethoxam, so use one or the other, not one after the other; toxic to bees - do not spray on open flowers; only where the label lists your crop; install yellow sticky traps to monitor.

healthy.name: Healthy
healthy.description: The leaf shows no sign of disease, pest or nutrient problem. Keep up regular field scouting.
symptoms: Uniform green trifoliate leaves
No spots, yellow patches, crinkling or holes
Normal leaf size and steady new growth
healthy.action: Continue weekly scouting and watch for whiteflies in the first 40 days.
